name: My Account
description: The authenticated member portal where members manage their products, payments, personal details, and membership benefits.

stages.name: Log In
stages.description: Member navigates to login page and authenticates
actions: Select Log in to My Account

painPoints.description: No social login option (Google, Apple). Users must create and remember a separate RAA password
Login page has no indication of what My Account lets you do, reducing motivation for first-time visitors
Forgot password flow requires email verification which can take 30-60 seconds, causing abandonment

opportunities.description: Add social login (Google, Apple) to reduce friction and eliminate password management
Add value proposition messaging on login page explaining what members can do in My Account

stages.name: My Account Home
stages.description: Member lands on dashboard showing their products, quick actions, and membership summary
thoughts: I need to update my payment details

painPoints.description: Products are listed without visual hierarchy. Car insurance policies look identical, differentiated only by rego number
Quick action cards are not personalised. All members see the same 4 actions regardless of their situation
Cross-sell banner for car insurance appears even for members who already have car insurance

opportunities.description: Add vehicle images or colour-coded tags to differentiate multiple car insurance policies
Personalise quick actions based on member context (upcoming renewal, recent claim, payment due)
Suppress cross-sell for products the member already holds

stages.name: Manage Personal Details
stages.description: Member updates their personal information, payment details, or communication preferences
thoughts: How do I change my address?
Is my payment card up to date?

painPoints.description: Changing address requires updating it separately for membership AND each insurance policy. Not synced.
No confirmation email or notification after updating payment details, causing anxiety about whether it worked
Communication preferences page has 8 different toggles with no clear explanation of what each controls

opportunities.description: Sync address changes across membership and all policies in a single update
Send confirmation email after any detail change with a summary of what was updated

stages.name: View My Products
stages.description: Member browses their product portfolio, views policy details, and manages individual products
actions: Click View details on a product

painPoints.description: Policy detail pages show raw policy numbers and dates without context. Members don't know what their excess is without clicking through multiple pages.
No way to compare two products side by side (e.g. comparing home vs contents cover)

opportunities.description: Add a summary card at the top of each product detail page showing the key information at a glance (excess, premium, renewal date, cover level)

stages.name: Member Benefits & Rewards
stages.description: Member discovers and accesses their membership benefits, discounts, and rewards
thoughts: Is this worth my membership fee?
How do I use my card?

painPoints.description: Benefits section is below the fold on the dashboard. Most users don't scroll past their products.
Clicking RAA Rewards or competitions opens in a new tab on an external site, losing the My Account context

opportunities.description: Surface a personalised 'Top benefit for you' card higher on the dashboard based on member location and interests

insights.description: 34 support tickets in Q1 2026 were about address changes not syncing across policies. This is the single highest-volume complaint category for My Account.
6 of 8 participants in the March 2026 usability test expected social login on the login page. 3 attempted to click where a Google button would be.
Analytics show 62% of My Account sessions end on the dashboard without navigating deeper. Members check their summary and leave.
Members with 3+ products spend 40% longer on the dashboard than single-product members, suggesting the product list becomes harder to parse at scale.
The cross-sell banner for car insurance was clicked by only 0.3% of members who already hold car insurance, indicating it adds clutter without value for existing customers.

changelog.description: Journey data published with full research findings, pain points, opportunities, and insights
